summary: A century-old lookout site whose 1958 cab burned in the 2002 Biscuit Fire and was rebuilt in 2004; now a Recreation.gov rental.

facts.status_note: Current structure is a 2004 rebuild after the prior cab burned in the 2002 Biscuit Fire.

access.note: Rentable via Recreation.gov; drive within sight of tower, then a 200-yard hike (final stretch closed to public vehicles); entry by combination lock.

visit.trail_note: Drive to within sight of the lookout, then hike the final 200 yards (public vehicles not permitted on that stretch).

events.note: firelookout.com dates the site's origin to a 1910 tent camp; NHLR instead dates the first lookout to 1917. Sources disagree.
NHLR states the first lookout was constructed in 1917.
firelookout.com states a 14x14-ft cabin was constructed in 1924.
Present (pre-2002) R-6 flat cab constructed, per both NHLR and firelookout.com.
Registered on the National Historic Lookout Register, April 1, 1991.
Lookout destroyed by the Biscuit Fire in August 2002.
Replacement rental cabin built two years after the fire.
Chetco Bar Fire also left visible effects on the surrounding landscape.

evidence.supports: first lookout year and NHLR registration date
evidence.quote: The first Lookout was constructed in 1917, and the present Lookout was constructed in 1958.

evidence.supports: third structure, WWII Aircraft Warning Service use, Biscuit Fire destruction and rebuild
evidence.quote: The fire lookout is the most recent of three structures built atop Snow Camp Mountain. The structures onsite were used as fire lookouts and an Aircraft Warning System station during World War II. The original cabin was destroyed in the 2002 Biscuit Fire, a massive blaze that burned more than a half-million acres in Oregon and California, but was reconstructed just two years later.

evidence.supports: coastal view and visible fire effects
evidence.quote: On a clear day, guests at Snow Camp Lookout will see ocean waves crashing along Kellogg Beach, Point St. George and Castle Rock near Crescent City, California.

evidence.supports: access via hike and combination lock
evidence.quote: Although visitors can drive within sight of the lookout, the 200-yard hike to the summit can be strenuous when carrying gear. The final 200 yards to the lookout are open to administrative traffic only.

evidence.supports: tent camp origin, 1924 cabin, 1958 R-6 flat, fire destruction, 2004 replacement
evidence.quote: Established with a tent camp in 1910, a 14x14' cab was constructed in 1924. An R-6 flat cab, built in 1958, was available on the Recreation Rental program and listed on the National Historic Lookout Register. It burned in an August 2002 forest fire. A replacement rental cabin was built in 2004.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: NHLR dates the first lookout to 1917; firelookout.com instead describes an earlier 1910 tent camp followed by a 1924 cabin. The story presents both without resolving which is more authoritative.

sources.title: Snow Camp Lookout, Rogue River-Siskiyou National Forest

notes_for_editor: Brief listed 'built 1924' as the headline build event, but that appears to be the second (cabin) structure per firelookout.com, not the first (1910 tent camp) or the current (2004) building. NHLR's 1917 first-lookout date conflicts with firelookout.com's 1910 tent camp. Elevation in brief (1268.3m) matches NHLR's 4,161 ft / 1,268 m; recreation.gov states 4,223 ft, a minor discrepancy not resolved here. Fact-check 2026-10-04: story and evidence all checked out against source text; only fix was adding a missing footnote on the sentence naming the 15x15 cabin and the Gold Beach Ranger District (was previously uncited) and adding the footnote URL list, which the story file was missing entirely.
